title: HELIX Govern: GLBA Compliance Scanner
description: Executable audit rules for detecting GLBA non-compliance across a HELIX-conformant medallion lakehouse. Companion to glba-safeguards-framework.json: that document defines WHAT must be done; this document provides HOW to detect what ISN'T done. Each rule includes a testable query or metadata check, severity, remediation, regulatory citation, and platform-specific implementation notes.
purpose: Scan a HELIX lakehouse for GLBA Safeguards Rule (16 CFR Part 314) non-compliance. Covers encryption at rest, encryption in transit, access control, data inventory completeness, monitoring, disposal, and service provider oversight. Intended to be run quarterly at minimum, with critical rules run on every deployment.

covered_resources: AidApplication (FAFSA/ISIR: SAI, ISIR transaction, comment codes, C-flags, NSLDS match flags)
Disbursement (individual aid disbursement and refund amounts)
LoanRecord (individual loan amounts, COD loan IDs)
Person (identifiers[] where type is national_id or ssn_last4)
ARTransaction (student billing when tied to financial aid disbursement)
covered_data_elements: tax_return_data (AGI, tax filing status, untaxed income)
scope.note: Every rule checks all tables in glba_tables. Where a platform example shows a single table (for example SHOW TBLPROPERTIES), run it for each table in the list. Query-text checks on 'disbursement' can match unrelated queries, so review hits before escalating.

scan_categories.description: GLBA-covered data must be encrypted at rest using a dedicated KMS key, separate from keys used for confidential or internal data. This ensures crypto-shredding is possible without affecting non-GLBA data.

rules.name: GLBA tables must use dedicated KMS encryption key
rules.description: All tables containing GLBA-covered data must be encrypted with a KMS key dedicated to restricted-tier data, separate from confidential-tier keys. This enables independent crypto-shredding and key rotation.

check_sql.ansi:
-- Verify encryption key assignment for GLBA tables
-- Requires platform-specific metadata views (see platform notes)
SELECT
  t.table_schema,
  t.table_name,
  t.encryption_key_id,
  CASE
    WHEN t.encryption_key_id = :restricted_kms_key_arn THEN 'PASS'
    WHEN t.encryption_key_id IS NULL THEN 'FAIL_NO_ENCRYPTION'
    ELSE 'FAIL_WRONG_KEY'
  END AS check_result
FROM information_schema.tables t
WHERE t.table_name IN (
  'fin_aid_award', 'aid_application', 'aid_package', 'verification', 'disbursement', 'loan_record', 'return_of_title_iv',
  'person',           -- only financial-identifier columns
  'ar_transaction'    -- student billing subset
)
AND t.table_schema IN ('bronze', 'silver', 'gold');
check_sql.snowflake:
SELECT
  table_catalog, table_schema, table_name,
  -- Snowflake encrypts all data; check is whether the table
  -- resides in a schema with the correct encryption policy
  'CHECK_MANUALLY' AS encryption_note
FROM snowflake.account_usage.tables
WHERE table_name IN ('FIN_AID_AWARD','PERSON','AR_TRANSACTION')
AND deleted IS NULL;
check_sql.redshift:
SELECT
  schemaname, tablename,
  -- Redshift uses cluster-level encryption; verify via
  -- SELECT encrypted FROM stv_startup_recovery_state;
  'CHECK_CLUSTER_ENCRYPTION' AS note
FROM pg_tables
WHERE tablename IN ('fin_aid_award', 'aid_application', 'aid_package', 'verification', 'disbursement', 'loan_record', 'return_of_title_iv', 'person', 'ar_transaction');
check_sql.bigquery:
SELECT
  table_id, kms_key_name,
  CASE WHEN kms_key_name = @restricted_key THEN 'PASS' ELSE 'FAIL' END AS check_result
FROM `project.dataset.__TABLES__`
WHERE table_id IN ('fin_aid_award', 'aid_application', 'aid_package', 'verification', 'disbursement', 'loan_record', 'return_of_title_iv', 'person', 'ar_transaction');

rules.expected_result: All GLBA tables use the restricted-tier KMS key ARN
rules.finding_if_failed: Table '{schema}.{table_name}' uses {encryption_key_id} instead of the dedicated restricted-tier KMS key
rules.remediation: Re-encrypt the table with the restricted-tier KMS key. For S3/Iceberg: update the table's storage encryption configuration and rewrite data files. For Snowflake: tables are encrypted by default but ensure the storage integration uses the correct key. For Redshift: the entire cluster must use encryption — cannot be per-table.

rules.name: No GLBA data in unencrypted staging areas
rules.description: Scan for GLBA-covered column names appearing in temporary, staging, or scratch schemas that may not have encryption policies applied.

check_sql.ansi:
SELECT
  c.table_schema,
  c.table_name,
  c.column_name
FROM information_schema.columns c
WHERE c.column_name IN (
  'sai', 'efc', 'expected_family_contribution', 'student_aid_index',
  'family_income', 'parent_income', 'parent_assets',
  'bank_account', 'bank_account_number', 'routing_number',
  'ssn', 'social_security_number', 'tax_id',
  'agi', 'adjusted_gross_income', 'tax_filing_status',
  'fafsa_transaction_number', 'isir_data',
  'loan_servicer_account', 'disbursement_amount'
)
AND c.table_schema NOT IN ('bronze', 'silver', 'gold')
ORDER BY c.table_schema, c.table_name;

rules.expected_result: Zero rows — no GLBA columns exist outside governed schemas
rules.finding_if_failed: GLBA-covered column '{column_name}' found in ungoverned location '{schema}.{table_name}'
rules.remediation: Move data to a governed schema with proper encryption and access controls, or drop the ungoverned copy. Investigate how GLBA data reached this location.

rules.name: No GLBA data in unencrypted export files
rules.description: Check for CSV, Parquet, or JSON export files containing GLBA data that were written to unencrypted storage (e.g., an S3 bucket without default encryption, a local file share).

check_sql.ansi:
-- Check for recent COPY/UNLOAD commands that wrote GLBA tables to external storage
SELECT
  query_id,
  query_text,
  start_time,
  user_name
FROM query_history
WHERE LOWER(query_text) LIKE '%unload%fin_aid_award%'
   OR LOWER(query_text) LIKE '%copy into%fin_aid_award%'
   OR LOWER(query_text) LIKE '%export%fin_aid_award%'
ORDER BY start_time DESC
LIMIT 100;
check_sql.snowflake:
SELECT
  query_id, query_text, start_time, user_name, role_name
FROM snowflake.account_usage.query_history
WHERE (LOWER(query_text) LIKE '%copy into%@%' OR LOWER(query_text) LIKE '%unload%')
AND ((LOWER(query_text) LIKE '%fin_aid_award%' OR LOWER(query_text) LIKE '%aid_application%' OR LOWER(query_text) LIKE '%aid_package%' OR LOWER(query_text) LIKE '%loan_record%' OR LOWER(query_text) LIKE '%return_of_title_iv%' OR LOWER(query_text) LIKE '%disbursement%')
     OR LOWER(query_text) LIKE '%sai%'
     OR LOWER(query_text) LIKE '%efc%')
AND start_time > DATEADD('day', -90, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP())
ORDER BY start_time DESC;

rules.expected_result: Zero unauthorized exports, or all exports target encrypted destinations
rules.finding_if_failed: GLBA data exported by '{user_name}' at {start_time} — verify destination encryption
rules.remediation: Audit the export destination. If unencrypted, delete the export file immediately and re-export to an encrypted location. Add an alert rule to prevent future unencrypted exports.

scan_categories.description: All connections transmitting GLBA data must use TLS 1.2 or higher. Unencrypted protocols (FTP, HTTP, SMTP without TLS) must never carry GLBA data.

rules.name: Database connections require TLS 1.2+
rules.description: All database connections to schemas containing GLBA data must enforce TLS 1.2 or higher. Connections using TLS 1.0/1.1 or no TLS must be rejected.

check_sql.snowflake:
-- Snowflake enforces TLS 1.2 by default on all connections.
-- Verify network policy doesn't allow exceptions:
SHOW NETWORK POLICIES;
-- Check that ALLOWED_IP_LIST doesn't bypass TLS requirements
check_sql.redshift:
-- Check cluster parameter group for require_ssl
SELECT name, setting
FROM pg_settings
WHERE name = 'ssl'
-- Must return 'on'
UNION ALL
SELECT 'min_tls', '1.2';  -- verify in parameter group
check_sql.bigquery:
-- BigQuery enforces TLS 1.2+ on all connections by default.
-- Verify VPC Service Controls are configured for the GLBA dataset:
-- Check via gcloud: gcloud access-context-manager perimeters list

rules.expected_result: TLS 1.2+ enforced on all database connections
rules.finding_if_failed: Database allows connections below TLS 1.2
rules.remediation: Update database/cluster configuration to require TLS 1.2 minimum. For Redshift: set require_ssl=true and ssl_min_protocol_version=TLSv1.2 in the parameter group.

rules.name: No GLBA data via unencrypted protocols
rules.description: Scan network/firewall logs for GLBA data transmitted via FTP (port 21), HTTP (port 80), or unencrypted SMTP (port 25) instead of SFTP/FTPS, HTTPS, or SMTP+TLS.

check_sql.ansi:
-- This is a network-level check, not a database query.
-- Implementation: review firewall/VPC flow logs for connections
-- from GLBA data stores to ports 21 (FTP), 80 (HTTP), 25 (SMTP).
-- Alert on any match.
SELECT 'Review VPC flow logs / firewall logs for unencrypted traffic from GLBA data stores' AS action;

rules.expected_result: Zero connections from GLBA data stores over unencrypted protocols
rules.finding_if_failed: Unencrypted {protocol} connection detected from GLBA data store to {destination}
rules.remediation: Block the unencrypted port at the firewall/security group level. Migrate the integration to the encrypted equivalent (FTP→SFTP, HTTP→HTTPS).

rules.name: HELIX Connect API endpoints enforce HTTPS with HSTS
rules.description: Any HELIX Connect API endpoint that serves GLBA-covered data (e.g., /financial-aid, /ar-transactions) must enforce HTTPS and return Strict-Transport-Security headers.

check_sql.ansi:
-- Manual check: curl the API endpoint
-- curl -I https://helix-api.institution.edu/v1/financial-aid
-- Verify: Strict-Transport-Security header present
-- Verify: HTTP (port 80) returns 301 redirect to HTTPS
SELECT 'Test API endpoints with curl -I for HSTS header' AS action;

rules.expected_result: HSTS header present with max-age >= 31536000 (1 year)
rules.finding_if_failed: API endpoint {endpoint} missing HSTS header or allows HTTP access
rules.remediation: Configure the API gateway/load balancer to add Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains and redirect all HTTP to HTTPS.

scan_categories.description: GLBA data must use named-individual access grants (not broad role-based access). All grants must be reviewed periodically and revoked promptly upon separation.

rules.name: No broad role grants on GLBA tables
rules.description: GLBA data must not be accessible through generic roles (e.g., 'analyst', 'all_users', 'public'). Access must be granted to named individuals or to a dedicated restricted-access role with named membership.

check_sql.ansi:
SELECT
  grantee,
  table_schema,
  table_name,
  privilege_type
FROM information_schema.table_privileges
WHERE table_name IN ('fin_aid_award', 'aid_application', 'aid_package', 'verification', 'disbursement', 'loan_record', 'return_of_title_iv', 'person', 'ar_transaction')
AND grantee NOT IN (
  'helix_analyst_restricted',  -- dedicated named-membership role
  'helix_silver_engineer',
  'helix_bronze_loader'
)
ORDER BY grantee;
check_sql.snowflake:
SELECT
  grantee_name, privilege, table_schema, table_name, granted_by
FROM snowflake.account_usage.grants_to_roles
WHERE table_name IN ('FIN_AID_AWARD','PERSON','AR_TRANSACTION')
AND privilege IN ('SELECT','INSERT','UPDATE')
AND deleted_on IS NULL
AND grantee_name NOT IN ('HELIX_ANALYST_RESTRICTED','HELIX_SILVER_ENGINEER','HELIX_BRONZE_LOADER');
check_sql.redshift:
SELECT
  u.usename AS grantee,
  s.schemaname,
  s.tablename,
  HAS_TABLE_PRIVILEGE(u.usename, s.schemaname || '.' || s.tablename, 'SELECT') AS has_select
FROM pg_user u
CROSS JOIN pg_tables s
WHERE s.tablename IN ('fin_aid_award', 'aid_application', 'aid_package', 'verification', 'disbursement', 'loan_record', 'return_of_title_iv', 'person', 'ar_transaction')
AND HAS_TABLE_PRIVILEGE(u.usename, s.schemaname || '.' || s.tablename, 'SELECT') = true
ORDER BY u.usename;

rules.expected_result: Only authorized restricted-tier roles and named individuals have access
rules.finding_if_failed: Unauthorized role/user '{grantee}' has {privilege_type} access to GLBA table '{table_name}'
rules.remediation: REVOKE {privilege_type} ON {table_name} FROM {grantee}; Investigate how the grant was created and establish a preventive control.

rules.name: Access review currency — GLBA grants reviewed within 90 days
rules.description: All active access grants to GLBA data must have been reviewed (approved or re-certified) within the last 90 days.

check_sql.ansi:
-- Requires an access_review_log table maintained by governance process
SELECT
  g.grantee,
  g.table_name,
  g.granted_on,
  r.last_review_date,
  DATEDIFF('day', r.last_review_date, CURRENT_DATE) AS days_since_review
FROM glba_grants g
LEFT JOIN access_review_log r
  ON g.grantee = r.grantee AND g.table_name = r.table_name
WHERE r.last_review_date IS NULL
   OR DATEDIFF('day', r.last_review_date, CURRENT_DATE) > 90;

rules.expected_result: Zero grants with reviews older than 90 days
rules.finding_if_failed: Grant for '{grantee}' on '{table_name}' has not been reviewed in {days_since_review} days
rules.remediation: Conduct an access review immediately. Re-certify the grant if still needed; revoke if not.

rules.name: No service accounts with GLBA access lacking an owner
rules.description: Service accounts (ETL, API, application accounts) with GLBA data access must each have a named human owner who is accountable for the account's activity.

check_sql.ansi:
-- Requires a service_account_registry table
SELECT
  sa.account_name,
  sa.purpose,
  sa.owner_name,
  sa.owner_email
FROM service_account_registry sa
WHERE sa.has_glba_access = true
AND (sa.owner_name IS NULL OR sa.owner_email IS NULL);

rules.expected_result: All GLBA service accounts have a named owner
rules.finding_if_failed: Service account '{account_name}' has GLBA access but no named owner
rules.remediation: Assign a named owner to the service account or revoke its GLBA access. Document the owner in the service account registry.

rules.name: Terminated employees have no active GLBA grants
rules.description: Cross-reference active GLBA access grants against the HR separation feed. Any employee who has separated should have GLBA grants revoked within 24 hours.

check_sql.ansi:
SELECT
  g.grantee AS db_user,
  e.employee_id,
  e.termination_date,
  DATEDIFF('day', e.termination_date, CURRENT_DATE) AS days_since_term
FROM glba_grants g
JOIN silver.employee e
  ON LOWER(g.grantee) = LOWER(e.username)
WHERE e.employment_status = 'terminated'
AND g.is_active = true;

rules.expected_result: Zero active GLBA grants for terminated employees
rules.finding_if_failed: CRITICAL: Terminated employee '{db_user}' (separated {days_since_term} days ago) still has active GLBA access
rules.remediation: Immediately revoke all database grants. Audit access logs since termination date for unauthorized access. Report as a potential incident.

rules.name: MFA required on all GLBA access paths
rules.description: Verify that multi-factor authentication is enforced for all authentication paths that lead to GLBA data (direct database, BI tool, API, SSH tunnel).

check_sql.ansi:
-- Check IdP/SSO configuration for MFA enforcement
-- This is typically checked via the identity provider admin console, not SQL.
-- For database-native auth:
SELECT
  username,
  authentication_method,
  mfa_enabled
FROM user_authentication_config
WHERE username IN (
  SELECT grantee FROM glba_grants WHERE is_active = true
)
AND (mfa_enabled = false OR mfa_enabled IS NULL);
check_sql.snowflake:
-- Check Snowflake network policy for MFA
SHOW PARAMETERS LIKE 'CLIENT_SESSION_KEEP_ALIVE' IN ACCOUNT;
-- Check that SSO/SAML is configured with MFA from the IdP side
-- Snowflake MFA: SHOW USERS; look for has_mfa = 'true'

rules.expected_result: MFA enabled for all users with GLBA access
rules.finding_if_failed: User '{username}' has GLBA access without MFA enabled
rules.remediation: Enable MFA for the user or enforce MFA at the IdP level. Block access until MFA is configured.

scan_categories.description: Maintain a complete inventory of where GLBA data is collected, stored, and transmitted. The HELIX data dictionary is the source of truth; actual lakehouse state must match.

rules.name: Data dictionary GLBA flags match actual schema
rules.description: Every field flagged glba=true in the HELIX data dictionary must exist as a column in the lakehouse. Every GLBA-covered column in the lakehouse must be flagged in the data dictionary.

check_sql.ansi:
-- Compare data dictionary to actual schema
-- Step 1: Fields in dictionary flagged GLBA but missing from lakehouse
SELECT dd.term, dd.resource, 'IN_DICTIONARY_NOT_IN_DB' AS gap_type
FROM helix_data_dictionary dd
WHERE dd.glba = true
AND NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns c
  WHERE LOWER(c.column_name) = LOWER(dd.term)
  AND LOWER(c.table_name) = LOWER(dd.resource)
)
UNION ALL
-- Step 2: Columns with GLBA-pattern names not in dictionary
SELECT c.column_name, c.table_name, 'IN_DB_NOT_IN_DICTIONARY' AS gap_type
FROM information_schema.columns c
WHERE c.column_name IN ('sai','efc','bank_account','routing_number','ssn','family_income','parent_income','parent_assets','tax_id','agi')
AND NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM helix_data_dictionary dd
  WHERE dd.glba = true
  AND LOWER(dd.term) = LOWER(c.column_name)
  AND LOWER(dd.resource) = LOWER(c.table_name)
);

rules.expected_result: Zero gaps — dictionary and lakehouse are in sync
rules.finding_if_failed: Gap: '{term}' in '{resource}' — {gap_type}
rules.remediation: Update the data dictionary to match the lakehouse (if the lakehouse is correct) or update the lakehouse to match the dictionary (if data was added without governance).

rules.name: No GLBA data in undocumented locations
rules.description: Scan ALL schemas (including temp, staging, sandbox, user-created) for columns matching GLBA field name patterns. Any GLBA data outside bronze/silver/gold is a potential compliance gap.

check_sql.ansi:
SELECT
  c.table_schema,
  c.table_name,
  c.column_name,
  'UNDOCUMENTED_GLBA_DATA' AS finding
FROM information_schema.columns c
WHERE c.column_name IN (
  'sai','efc','expected_family_contribution','student_aid_index',
  'family_income','parent_income','parent_assets',
  'bank_account','bank_account_number','routing_number',
  'ssn','social_security_number','tax_id',
  'agi','adjusted_gross_income','fafsa_transaction_number'
)
AND c.table_schema NOT IN ('bronze','silver','gold','information_schema')
ORDER BY c.table_schema, c.table_name;

rules.expected_result: Zero rows — no GLBA data outside governed schemas
rules.finding_if_failed: Undocumented GLBA column '{column_name}' found in '{table_schema}.{table_name}'
rules.remediation: Investigate origin. Drop if unauthorized copy. If legitimate, move to governed schema and document in data dictionary.

scan_categories.description: All access to GLBA data must be logged with full query text. Logs must be retained for 7+ years. Anomalous access must trigger real-time alerts.

rules.name: All reads of GLBA tables are logged with query text
rules.description: Verify that query history / access history captures every SELECT against GLBA tables, including the full query text, user identity, timestamp, and rows returned.

check_sql.snowflake:
-- Verify access history is capturing GLBA table reads
SELECT COUNT(*) AS glba_queries_last_24h
FROM snowflake.account_usage.access_history
WHERE ARRAY_CONTAINS('FIN_AID_AWARD'::VARIANT, base_objects_accessed:objectName)
AND query_start_time > DATEADD('hour', -24, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP());
check_sql.redshift:
-- Verify STL_QUERY or SYS_QUERY_HISTORY captures GLBA queries
SELECT COUNT(*) AS glba_queries_last_24h
FROM stl_query
WHERE (LOWER(querytxt) LIKE '%fin_aid_award%' OR LOWER(querytxt) LIKE '%aid_application%' OR LOWER(querytxt) LIKE '%aid_package%' OR LOWER(querytxt) LIKE '%loan_record%' OR LOWER(querytxt) LIKE '%return_of_title_iv%' OR LOWER(querytxt) LIKE '%disbursement%')
AND starttime > GETDATE() - INTERVAL '24 hours';
check_sql.ansi:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS glba_queries_last_24h
FROM query_history
WHERE (LOWER(query_text) LIKE '%fin_aid_award%' OR LOWER(query_text) LIKE '%aid_application%' OR LOWER(query_text) LIKE '%aid_package%' OR LOWER(query_text) LIKE '%loan_record%' OR LOWER(query_text) LIKE '%return_of_title_iv%' OR LOWER(query_text) LIKE '%disbursement%')
AND start_time > CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - INTERVAL '24' HOUR;

rules.expected_result: Count > 0 if GLBA tables were queried (confirms logging is active). If count = 0 and tables were queried, logging is broken.
rules.finding_if_failed: Query logging is not capturing GLBA table access
rules.remediation: Enable query history / access history logging. For Snowflake: this is automatic in Enterprise+. For Redshift: ensure STL logging is not disabled. For BigQuery: audit logs are automatic.

rules.name: Anomalous access detection — bulk GLBA reads
rules.description: Flag queries that return an unusually high number of GLBA records (more than 1000 rows in a single query). Normal operations rarely need bulk access to GLBA data.

check_sql.snowflake:
SELECT
  user_name,
  query_id,
  query_text,
  rows_produced,
  query_start_time
FROM snowflake.account_usage.query_history
WHERE ((LOWER(query_text) LIKE '%fin_aid_award%' OR LOWER(query_text) LIKE '%aid_application%' OR LOWER(query_text) LIKE '%aid_package%' OR LOWER(query_text) LIKE '%loan_record%' OR LOWER(query_text) LIKE '%return_of_title_iv%' OR LOWER(query_text) LIKE '%disbursement%')
       OR LOWER(query_text) LIKE '%sai%'
       OR LOWER(query_text) LIKE '%efc%')
AND rows_produced > 1000
AND query_start_time > DATEADD('day', -7, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP())
ORDER BY rows_produced DESC;
check_sql.ansi:
SELECT
  user_name, query_id, query_text, rows_returned, start_time
FROM query_history
WHERE table_accessed IN ('fin_aid_award', 'aid_application', 'aid_package', 'verification', 'disbursement', 'loan_record', 'return_of_title_iv', 'person', 'ar_transaction')
AND rows_returned > 1000
AND start_time > CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - INTERVAL '7' DAY
ORDER BY rows_returned DESC;

rules.expected_result: Zero bulk reads, or all bulk reads are from authorized batch processes
rules.finding_if_failed: User '{user_name}' retrieved {rows_produced} GLBA records at {query_start_time}. Query: {query_text}
rules.remediation: Investigate the query. If unauthorized bulk export, treat as a potential data incident. If authorized ETL, document in the authorized_batch_processes list.

rules.name: GLBA access log retention — 7+ years
rules.description: Verify that GLBA access logs are retained for at least 7 years. Check the oldest available log entry for GLBA tables.

check_sql.snowflake:
-- Snowflake account_usage retains 365 days by default.
-- For 7-year retention, logs must be exported to long-term storage.
SELECT
  MIN(query_start_time) AS oldest_log_entry,
  DATEDIFF('day', MIN(query_start_time), CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()) AS retention_days
FROM snowflake.account_usage.query_history
WHERE (LOWER(query_text) LIKE '%fin_aid_award%' OR LOWER(query_text) LIKE '%aid_application%' OR LOWER(query_text) LIKE '%aid_package%' OR LOWER(query_text) LIKE '%loan_record%' OR LOWER(query_text) LIKE '%return_of_title_iv%' OR LOWER(query_text) LIKE '%disbursement%');
check_sql.ansi:
SELECT
  MIN(start_time) AS oldest_log,
  DATEDIFF('day', MIN(start_time), CURRENT_DATE) AS retention_days
FROM query_history
WHERE table_accessed IN ('fin_aid_award', 'aid_application', 'aid_package', 'verification', 'disbursement', 'loan_record', 'return_of_title_iv');

rules.expected_result: Retention >= 2555 days (7 years), OR confirmed export to long-term archive
rules.finding_if_failed: GLBA access logs only retained for {retention_days} days — below 7-year requirement
rules.remediation: Configure log export to long-term storage (S3 Glacier, Azure Archive, GCS Archive) with a 7-year lifecycle policy. Implement a nightly export job.

rules.name: After-hours GLBA access alerting
rules.description: Verify that an alert is configured to notify the Qualified Individual when GLBA data is accessed outside normal business hours (before 7 AM or after 7 PM local time, weekends, holidays).

check_sql.ansi:
-- Check for after-hours GLBA access in the last 30 days
SELECT
  user_name,
  query_id,
  start_time,
  EXTRACT(HOUR FROM start_time) AS hour_of_day,
  EXTRACT(DOW FROM start_time) AS day_of_week
FROM query_history
WHERE table_accessed IN ('fin_aid_award', 'aid_application', 'aid_package', 'verification', 'disbursement', 'loan_record', 'return_of_title_iv', 'person', 'ar_transaction')
AND (
  EXTRACT(HOUR FROM start_time) < 7
  OR EXTRACT(HOUR FROM start_time) > 19
  OR EXTRACT(DOW FROM start_time) IN (0, 6)  -- Sunday, Saturday
)
AND start_time > CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - INTERVAL '30' DAY
ORDER BY start_time DESC;

rules.expected_result: Zero after-hours access, or all flagged access has documented justification
rules.finding_if_failed: After-hours GLBA access by '{user_name}' at {start_time} — verify this was authorized
rules.remediation: Configure an automated alert (SNS, PagerDuty, email) that fires on after-hours GLBA queries. Investigate any unauthorized access.

scan_categories.description: GLBA data must be disposed of no later than two years after the last use, unless retention is otherwise required. Disposal means crypto-shredding across all copies.

rules.name: GLBA data past retention period identified
rules.description: Identify GLBA records where the student's last enrollment/aid year plus the retention period has passed. Federal regulations require retention through the end of the award year plus the audit resolution period (typically 3 years after the close of the award year).

check_sql.ansi:
SELECT
  fa.helix_id,
  fa.student_ref,
  fa.academic_period_ref,
  fa.award_year,
  DATEDIFF('year', fa.award_year_end_date, CURRENT_DATE) AS years_since_award_year_end
FROM silver.fin_aid_award fa
WHERE DATEDIFF('year', fa.award_year_end_date, CURRENT_DATE) > 6
-- 3 years post-award-year for federal retention + 3 year buffer
AND fa.disposal_status IS NULL
ORDER BY fa.award_year_end_date ASC;

rules.expected_result: All records past retention are flagged for disposal review
rules.finding_if_failed: {count} GLBA records past retention period without disposal flag
rules.remediation: Flag records for disposal review by the Data Steward. Upon approval, crypto-shred with certificate of destruction.

rules.name: Disposed GLBA data has certificate of destruction
rules.description: Every GLBA disposal action must be documented with a certificate recording: what was destroyed, when, by whom, method (crypto-shred, overwrite), and confirmation that backups were also destroyed.

check_sql.ansi:
SELECT
  d.disposal_id,
  d.resource_name,
  d.records_destroyed,
  d.disposal_date,
  d.disposed_by,
  d.method,
  d.backup_confirmed_destroyed,
  d.certificate_on_file
FROM disposal_log d
WHERE d.resource_name IN ('fin_aid_award', 'aid_application', 'aid_package', 'verification', 'disbursement', 'loan_record', 'return_of_title_iv', 'person', 'ar_transaction')
AND (d.certificate_on_file = false OR d.backup_confirmed_destroyed = false);

rules.expected_result: All disposals have certificates and backup confirmation
rules.finding_if_failed: Disposal {disposal_id} on {disposal_date} missing certificate or backup confirmation
rules.remediation: Complete the certificate of destruction. Verify backup copies were also destroyed and document the verification.

scan_categories.description: Select and retain service providers capable of maintaining safeguards. Contractually require safeguards. Periodically assess compliance.

rules.name: All vendors with GLBA data access have current DSA
rules.description: Every third-party vendor, cloud provider, or contractor with access to GLBA data must have a current, signed data sharing agreement (DSA) that includes GLBA safeguards provisions.

check_sql.ansi:
SELECT
  v.vendor_name,
  v.service_description,
  v.has_glba_data_access,
  v.dsa_signed_date,
  v.dsa_expiration_date,
  CASE
    WHEN v.dsa_expiration_date < CURRENT_DATE THEN 'EXPIRED'
    WHEN v.dsa_signed_date IS NULL THEN 'NO_DSA'
    ELSE 'CURRENT'
  END AS dsa_status
FROM vendor_registry v
WHERE v.has_glba_data_access = true
AND (v.dsa_expiration_date < CURRENT_DATE OR v.dsa_signed_date IS NULL);

rules.expected_result: All GLBA vendors have current DSAs
rules.finding_if_failed: Vendor '{vendor_name}' has GLBA access with {dsa_status} data sharing agreement
rules.remediation: Execute or renew the DSA immediately. If vendor refuses GLBA terms, terminate their access to GLBA data. Reference govern/data-sharing-agreement-template.json for the required provisions.

rules.name: Vendor security assessments current within 12 months
rules.description: Each vendor with GLBA access must have a security assessment (SOC 2, HECVAT, or equivalent) on file that is no older than 12 months.

check_sql.ansi:
SELECT
  v.vendor_name,
  v.last_security_assessment_date,
  v.assessment_type,
  DATEDIFF('month', v.last_security_assessment_date, CURRENT_DATE) AS months_since_assessment
FROM vendor_registry v
WHERE v.has_glba_data_access = true
AND (
  v.last_security_assessment_date IS NULL
  OR DATEDIFF('month', v.last_security_assessment_date, CURRENT_DATE) > 12
);

rules.expected_result: All GLBA vendors assessed within 12 months
rules.finding_if_failed: Vendor '{vendor_name}' last assessed {months_since_assessment} months ago (or never assessed)
rules.remediation: Request updated SOC 2 Type II or HECVAT from the vendor. If not available within 30 days, escalate to the Qualified Individual for risk acceptance or access termination.

finding_format.description: Each finding produced by the scanner follows this structure

schema.rule_id: string — the rule that generated this finding
schema.layer: bronze | silver | gold | transport | backup | governance
schema.detail: string — specific finding description with interpolated values
schema.tested_by: string — scanner version, auditor name, or automated job ID

summary_format.description: Aggregate scan results for dashboards and reporting

annual_board_report_template.description: Template for the Qualified Individual's annual report to the governing board per 16 CFR 314.4(i). Must be in writing and cover all required elements.

sections.content: Summary of the institution's GLBA information security program, including the designated Qualified Individual, program scope, and organizational structure.
Summary of the most recent written risk assessment (314.4(b)): key risks identified, risk ratings (likelihood × impact), and changes from the prior assessment.
HELIX GLBA Scanner summary: total rules tested, pass/fail counts by category (encryption, access control, monitoring, disposal, vendor oversight), compliance score, trend vs. prior quarter/year.

Summary of any security incidents involving GLBA-covered data: number of incidents, nature (unauthorized access, data breach, lost device, phishing), individuals affected, notification actions taken (FTC 30-day rule for 500+ consumers), remediation status.
Status of all open remediation items from prior scans: items closed, items still open, items overdue, root cause analysis for recurring findings.
Summary of annual penetration test and semi-annual vulnerability assessments (314.4(d)): findings, severity, remediation status.
Percentage of employees who completed security awareness training. Completion rate for specialized GLBA training for financial aid and data engineering staff.
Number of vendors with GLBA access, DSA status (current/expired/missing), most recent security assessments, any vendor-related incidents.
Any material changes to the information security program since the last report: new systems, vendor changes, organizational changes, regulatory updates.
Qualified Individual's recommendations for program improvements, resource requests, and risk acceptance decisions requiring board approval.

implementation_notes.automation: Deploy scanner rules as scheduled SQL tasks (Snowflake Tasks, Redshift Scheduled Queries, Databricks Jobs, BigQuery Scheduled Queries) running at least quarterly. Critical rules (EAR-001, AC-004, EIT-001) should run daily.
implementation_notes.integration: Scanner findings can be exported as JSON and ingested into GRC tools (ServiceNow GRC, Archer, LogicGate) or ticketing systems for remediation tracking.
implementation_notes.testing: Before first production scan, validate each rule against a known-good environment (all passing) and a known-bad test environment (all failing) to confirm the scanner works correctly.
implementation_notes.customization: Institutions should customize: KMS key ARNs, schema names (if not bronze/silver/gold), authorized role names, retention periods (if state law requires longer than federal), business hours for after-hours alerting.

references: 16 CFR Part 314 — Standards for Safeguarding Customer Information (FTC Safeguards Rule)
